narrativeReportMd:
# Endpoint R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`Endpoint` has several local breaking changes. The highest-impact issues are the required `status` code-set change, the `connectionType` representation changing from a single `Coding` to repeating `CodeableConcept`, and the restructuring of direct payload fields into a new repeating `payload` backbone. These are not inherited base-artifact changes.

## Scope
The comparison used the supplied R4 and R6 core StructureDefinitions, package indexes/metadata, and locally available related terminology. The R6 `Endpoint` StructureDefinition is present under the same canonical URL, so this is a same-artifact comparison.

## Main migration themes
R4 instances cannot be accepted as R6 without structural transforms: `connectionType` must be wrapped into a `CodeableConcept`, and `payloadType`/`payloadMimeType` must be moved into `payload.type`/`payload.mimeType`. Terminology migration is also needed because R4 `status=test` is no longer in the required R6 EndpointStatus value set; R6 introduces `status=limited` and a separate `environmentType` element for dev/test/prod-like classification.

## Highest-impact findings
The strongest validation breaks are `Endpoint.status` and `Endpoint.connectionType`. Because `connectionType`, `status`, `address`, and in R4 `payloadType` are mandatory, these changes affect most complete Endpoint migrations rather than only edge cases.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for mapping `status=test`, deciding whether R6 `limited` maps to an R4 extension or local code, preserving payload profile semantics during down-conversion, and reinterpreting `managingOrganization` where implementations used it as a data-steward or owner reference.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several goals appear understandable: R6 supports richer endpoint classification, grouped payload metadata, profile-specific payload expectations, environment tagging, and explicit availability. The most disruptive changes could have been softened by keeping deprecated R4 elements or codes alongside the new model for at least one release.

## Follow-up analysis
Review base artifact reports for inherited Resource/DomainResource/Element changes, the new `Availability` datatype report for schedule semantics, and authoritative terminology expansions for external THO and v3 value sets.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `Endpoint` has hard local R4→R6 breaks in `status`, `connectionType`, and payload representation. The top migration concerns are mapping `status=test`, changing generated models/parsers for `connectionType` and `payload`, and preserving R6-only operational context such as `environmentType`, `availability`, and payload profiles when converting back to R4. Confidence is high for StructureDefinition-level changes and medium for external terminology nuance.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be transform-driven rather than a pure validator upgrade. R4 `connectionType` should become a one-entry R6 `CodeableConcept`; R4 payload fields should move under one or more `Endpoint.payload` entries; R4 `status=test` needs policy-based mapping, likely involving R6 `environmentType=test` and a non-test operational status. Down-conversion from R6 to R4 is lossy when multiple connection concepts, grouped payloads, payload profiles, availability schedules, or environment classifications are used.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for local element presence, cardinality, datatype, required binding, and code-system differences because they are directly present in the supplied StructureDefinitions and local complete EndpointStatus CodeSystems. Confidence is lower for exact terminology impact on example/extensible bindings because current external THO expansions and rendered narrative rationale were not available.

findings.title: Required Endpoint.status code set removes `test` and adds `limited`

oldState.summary: Mandatory code with required binding to EndpointStatus containing active, suspended, error, off, entered-in-error, and test.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The comparison used the complete local R4 and R6 `CodeSystem-endpoint-status.json` files, not a terminology server expansion.

flags.isModifierReason: This element is labelled as a modifier because it is a status element that contains status entered-in-error which means that the resource should not be treated as valid

semanticText.short: active | suspended | error | off | entered-in-error | test
semanticText.comment: This element is labeled as a modifier because the status contains codes that mark the endpoint as not currently valid.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `status` is mandatory and bound with required strength to the R4 EndpointStatus code system, including the `test` code.

newState.summary: Mandatory code with required binding to EndpointStatus containing active, limited, suspended, error, off, and entered-in-error.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 adds `limited` with semantics for limited availability/use, and no longer includes `test` in the complete EndpointStatus CodeSystem.

flags.isModifierReason: This element is labelled as a modifier because it is a status element that contains status entered-in-error which means that the resource should not be treated as valid

semanticText.short: active | limited | suspended | error | off | entered-in-error
semanticText.definition: The endpoint status represents whether the endpoint can currently be used for connections or why it can't be used.
semanticText.comment: This element is labeled as a modifier because the status contains codes that mark the endpoint as not currently valid. Temporary downtimes or other unexpected short-term changes in availability would not be represented in this property.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, `status` remains mandatory and modifier-significant, but the required value set changes by removing `test` and adding `limited`.

facts.note: R4-valid `Endpoint.status = test` is not in the R6 required value set.
R6-valid `Endpoint.status = limited` is not in the R4 required value set.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because the binding is required and `status` is mandatory, an R4 instance using `status: test` becomes invalid under the R6 EndpointStatus value set. Conversely, an R6 instance using `status: limited` is not valid R4 without an extension or local-code policy. Generated enum switches and business rules that distinguish test endpoints from unavailable endpoints need explicit migration logic.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Confusing a test, limited, active, or unavailable endpoint can cause clients to use the wrong service environment or avoid a service that is intended to be usable only under constraints.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate operational availability from environment classification and introduce a status for limited use.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `test` as a deprecated R6 status code while adding `limited` and `environmentType`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating operational availability from environment classification is a reasonable R6 goal, and adding `limited` plus `environmentType` supports that goal. The direct break comes from removing `test` from a required code system on a mandatory modifier element. Because R6 could have retained `test` as deprecated while steering new data to `environmentType=test` plus an operational status, the level of breakage looks probably avoidable rather than necessary.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design would keep `test` in `EndpointStatus` as deprecated or legacy-compatible, add `limited`, and document that new endpoints should represent non-production use with `environmentType`. That is not merely conversion tooling: it would preserve R4-valid `status=test` instances under R6 validation. The cost is that `status` would keep a legacy environment-like code during the transition, so enum handlers and business rules would still need to recognize and discourage it.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances but prolongs mixed environment/status semantics and requires consumers to handle a deprecated status code.

evidence.detail: R4 `Endpoint.status` is 1..1 `code` with required binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/endpoint-status|4.0.1` and short text listing `test`.
evidence.quote: active | suspended | error | off | entered-in-error | test

evidence.detail: R6 `Endpoint.status` is 1..1 `code` with required binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/endpoint-status|6.0.0-ballot4` and short text listing `limited` instead of `test`.
evidence.quote: active | limited | suspended | error | off | entered-in-error

evidence.detail: The complete local R4 CodeSystem includes `test`; the complete local R6 CodeSystem includes `limited` and omits `test`.
The R4 status ConceptMap maps `test` to resource-status `draft`; the R6 ConceptMap has no `test` mapping and maps `limited` to resource-status `partial`.

examples.examplesMd: The examples are focused fragments. A real migration must also transform `connectionType` and payload fields.

findings.narrativeMd: `Endpoint.status` is still a required, modifier-significant code, but the code system changed in a way that invalidates R4 test endpoints. This is a hard validation break because required bindings admit only listed codes. It is also a runtime break for generated enum types and switch statements that contained `test` or do not know `limited`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `status = test` can be valid in R4 but invalid in R6. R6 instances with `status = limited` cannot be represented as valid R4 Endpoint status without an extension, local convention, or lossy mapping. Strict validators and generated enum parsers will reject the unknown code in both directions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory endpoints with `status=test`. Decide whether they are usable but non-production (`status=active` or `limited` plus `environmentType=test`) or not currently usable (`status=off`, `suspended`, or `error`). Down-conversion should preserve `limited` in an extension or profile-specific code map rather than silently mapping it to `active`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The semantic split between endpoint environment and operational status is useful, but the same goal could have been achieved by retaining `test` as deprecated in the R6 required value set while encouraging `environmentType`. That would have preserved R4 instance validity while giving implementers a transition path.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is needed because `test` is not semantically identical to `limited`; the correct migration depends on whether the endpoint is non-production, partially available, internally tested, or intentionally disabled.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Endpoint.status` is mandatory, modifier-significant, and required-bound, so removing the R4 `test` code creates a direct validation and enum/API break. The R6 direction is understandable: environment classification now has its own element and `limited` describes constrained operational use. But the migration from `test` is policy-dependent, and keeping `test` as a deprecated legacy code would have preserved R4-valid instances while still steering new implementations to `environmentType`.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Endpoint.status` is 1..1 `code` with required binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/endpoint-status|4.0.1` and includes `test` in the listed status codes.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Endpoint.status` remains 1..1 `code` with required binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/endpoint-status|6.0.0-ballot4` and lists `limited` instead of `test`.
Local CodeSystem-endpoint-status files confirm R4 has `test`; R6 has `limited` and omits `test`.
R6 adds `Endpoint.environmentType` with an environment code `test`, supporting a status/environment split.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2 and trial-use status are neutral under the framework. They do not impose normative-level stability, but they also do not soften a mandatory required-bound modifier change enough to dismiss it.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with `status` = `test` fail R6 required-value-set validation; R6 `limited` also creates R6-to-R4 loss and generated enum/switch churn.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. R6 could keep `test` in EndpointStatus as deprecated or legacy-compatible while adding `limited` and `environmentType`. The tradeoff is continued support for a status code that blends environment with operational state, but that is a modest transitional cost compared with invalidating existing mandatory status values.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the prior report's high impact and Yes less-breaking alternative judgment match this independent assessment; the fresh-review action judgment is Revisit because the break is required-bound, mandatory, and avoidable.

findings.title: Endpoint.connectionType changes from a single Coding to repeating CodeableConcept

oldState.summary: Required 1..1 `Coding` with extensible binding to endpoint-connection-type.

semanticText.short: Protocol/Profile/Standard to be used with this endpoint connection
semanticText.definition: A coded value that represents the technical details of the usage of this endpoint, such as what WSDLs should be used in what way. (e.g. XDS.b/DICOM/cds-hook).
semanticText.comment: For additional connectivity details for the protocol, extensions will be used at this point, as in the XDS example.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, every Endpoint has exactly one `connectionType`, and the JSON/XML shape is the primitive FHIR `Coding` datatype.

newState.summary: Required 1..* `CodeableConcept` with example binding to endpoint-connection-type.

semanticText.short: Protocol/Profile/Standard to be used with this endpoint connection
semanticText.definition: A coded value that represents the technical details of the usage of this endpoint, such as what WSDLs should be used in what way. (e.g. XDS.b/DICOM/cds-hook).
semanticText.comment: For additional connectivity details for the protocol, extensions will be used at this point, as in the XDS example. If there are multiple payload types or mimetypes they are all applicable for all connection types, and all have the same status.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, Endpoint can have one or more `connectionType` entries, each a `CodeableConcept` that can carry multiple codings and text.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct wire-format and code-generation break. R4 JSON such as `connectionType: {system, code}` is a `Coding`; R6 expects an array of `CodeableConcept` objects with `coding` arrays. Because the element remains mandatory, most complete R4 Endpoint instances and generated R4 model classes require a transform.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The primary risk is technical interoperability failure. Business meaning can also be lost if multiple R6 concepts or free text are collapsed to one R4 coding.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow multiple protocol/profile classifications and richer coding/text representation for an endpoint.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 `connectionType` `Coding` and add a separate optional repeating richer connection-type element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is strong: endpoints may need multiple protocol/profile classifications and a richer `CodeableConcept` representation. A less-breaking design exists, but it would keep the old mandatory `Coding` beside a new richer representation for the same fact. That duplicate same-resource representation is a material long-term interoperability cost, so the breaking clean replacement is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would leave `Endpoint.connectionType` as the R4 `Coding` and introduce a new optional repeatable `CodeableConcept` element for richer or multiple connection classifications. Existing R4 instances would remain valid, but R6 consumers would have to merge two fields, decide precedence, and handle disagreement. The old representation also cannot carry multiple codings or text, so the alternative only covers common single-coding cases cleanly.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves the R4 wire shape for common cases but creates duplicate protocol-classification locations that can diverge and burden consumers.

connectionType.text: FHIR REST endpoint over mutual TLS

examples.examplesMd: The old fragment shows the R4 `Coding` shape. The migration wraps that coding inside a one-entry R6 `CodeableConcept` array.

findings.narrativeMd: `Endpoint.connectionType` keeps its name but changes datatype and multiplicity. This is easy to miss in path-based diffs because the path is unchanged, but the serialized shape and generated property type are incompatible. The binding is also weakened from extensible to example, which is not hard-breaking but changes conformance expectations.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A valid R4 instance with a `Coding` object at `connectionType` is not valid R6 because R6 expects repeating `CodeableConcept`. R6 content with multiple connection types, multiple codings, or `text` cannot be losslessly represented as R4's single `Coding`. Strict parsers, JSON schema validators, FHIRPath code that expects `connectionType.system`, and generated client models are affected.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4→R6, wrap the R4 coding into `connectionType[0].coding[0]`. For R6→R4, only a single unambiguous coding can be mapped losslessly; preserve additional codings, text, or additional connection types in extensions or flag for manual review. Update tests to cover single-coding, multi-coding, and multi-connection-type cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer R6 representation is useful, but replacing a mandatory datatype is disruptive. A backward-compatible transition could have added a new optional richer element and deprecated the old `Coding`, though that would require consumers to merge two representations.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Check generated model packages carefully; this is a same-path type replacement and may compile as a property type change rather than a missing/added field.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The unchanged path hides a real wire-shape and generated-model change: R4 has one mandatory `Coding`, while R6 has one or more `CodeableConcept` values. R4-to-R6 migration is usually mechanical for the common case by wrapping the coding, but strict parsers and generated clients still break. The R6 model supports multiple classifications, multiple codings, and text; preserving the old `Coding` beside the richer field would create duplicate protocol-classification locations with precedence and consistency problems.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Endpoint.connectionType` is 1..1 `Coding` with an extensible endpoint-connection-type binding.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Endpoint.connectionType` is 1..* `CodeableConcept` with an example endpoint-connection-type binding.
The element remains mandatory in both versions, so complete Endpoint instances and generated models must handle the changed shape.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2 and trial-use status are neutral. The decision rests mainly on the concrete codegen/wire-format break and on whether the richer R6 representation justifies it.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 `Coding` object at `connectionType` is not the R6 repeating `CodeableConcept` shape; generated property types and reverse conversion of multiple/textual R6 concepts are also affected.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could have retained the R4 `Coding` and added a new optional richer repeating element, but that would duplicate the same endpoint protocol fact and require rules for disagreement. It would preserve common R4 instances but would not cleanly meet the R6 goal.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the prior high impact and Partial alternative judgment are appropriate, but the break appears proportionate given the material cost of carrying both representations.

findings.title: R4 direct payload fields are replaced by an optional repeating Endpoint.payload backbone

oldState.summary: `payloadType` is a required direct child and `payloadMimeType` is an optional direct child.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R4 `ValueSet-endpoint-payload-type` includes the endpoint-payload-type CodeSystem and an inline set of IHE/v3-style format codes. No full expansion was available.

semanticText.short: The type of content that may be used at this endpoint (e.g. XDS Discharge summaries)
semanticText.definition: The payload type describes the acceptable content that can be communicated on the endpoint.
semanticText.comment: The payloadFormat describes the serialization format of the data, where the payloadType indicates the specific document/schema that is being transferred; e.g. DischargeSummary or CarePlan.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, payload metadata is split across direct fields: mandatory `payloadType` and optional `payloadMimeType`.

newState.summary: `payload` is a 0..* BackboneElement with optional `type`, `mimeType`, `profileCanonical`, and `profileUri` children.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 `ValueSet-endpoint-payload-type` includes the endpoint-payload-type CodeSystem and the external `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/v3-HL7FormatCodes` value set, so exact code-level differences require terminology expansion.

semanticText.short: Set of payloads that are provided by this endpoint
semanticText.definition: The set of payloads that are provided/available at this endpoint.
semanticText.comment: Note that not all mimetypes or types will be listed under the one endpoint resource, there may be multiple instances that information for cases where other header data such as the endpoint address, active status/period etc. is different.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, payload information is grouped under a new optional repeating backbone. `payload.type` and `payload.mimeType` are analogous to the old fields, but neither the group nor the type child is mandatory, and new profile fields have no R4 peer.

facts.note: R6 `Endpoint.payload.type` is optional inside an optional payload group.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old and new fields have matching definitions and bindings for type and MIME type, but R6 groups them inside a new `payload` backbone and adds profile-specific children.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `payloadType` is mandatory, so every complete R4 Endpoint instance contains an element that no longer exists at the top level in R6. R6 validators will reject untransformed R4 payload fields. R6 can also express payload groupings and profile expectations that R4 has no native elements for.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Payload type, MIME type, and profile metadata drive content negotiation and endpoint selection. Dropping or flattening them can cause clients to send or request unsupported content.

justification.inferredGoal: Group payload type, MIME type, and profile expectations and support endpoints with multiple payload descriptions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add the new `payload` backbone while retaining deprecated top-level `payloadType` and `payloadMimeType` for a transition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 payload backbone has a clear modeling goal: group payload type, MIME type, and profile expectations so multiple payload descriptions can be represented coherently. A transition model with both old and new fields would preserve many R4 instances, but it would duplicate the same payload facts and would not fully express grouping/profile semantics through the old flat fields. Those material tradeoffs make the breaking redesign probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design would keep `payloadType` and `payloadMimeType` as deprecated direct children and define them as mapping to a default `payload` entry. This would preserve common R4 data without a required transform. The tradeoff is indefinite duplicate representations: old flat fields and new grouped fields could disagree, consumers would need precedence rules, and profile-specific or multi-group R6 payloads would still not be cleanly represented by the old fields.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Reduces R4 wire-format breakage but creates duplicate payload metadata and consistency problems between flat and grouped forms.

evidence.detail: R4 `Endpoint.payloadType` is 1..* `CodeableConcept` with example binding to endpoint-payload-type.
R4 `Endpoint.payloadMimeType` is 0..* `code` with required binding to mimetypes.
R6 `Endpoint.payload.type` is 0..* `CodeableConcept` with example binding to endpoint-payload-type.
R6 adds payload profile fields that have no direct R4 Endpoint field.

examples.examplesMd: The old fragment shows top-level R4 payload fields. The migrated fragment places the analogous content inside one R6 `payload` entry. The R6 profile example cannot be represented in base R4 without an extension.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 replaces R4's direct payload fields with a nested repeating payload component. This is both a path change and a content-model change: R4 required at least one payload type, while R6 permits no payload group or payload group with MIME/profile information and no type. Implementers cannot rely on simple field renaming without considering grouping and cardinality.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Untransformed R4 instances with `payloadType` or `payloadMimeType` are invalid against R6 because those top-level paths are gone. R6 instances using `payload.profileCanonical`, `payload.profileUri`, multiple payload groups, or no payload type cannot be losslessly represented in R4's mandatory flat `payloadType` plus optional flat `payloadMimeType` model.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4→R6, create at least one `payload` entry and move `payloadType` to `payload.type` and `payloadMimeType` to `payload.mimeType`. If there are multiple payload types and MIME types, decide whether all combinations apply or whether multiple payload groups are needed. For R6→R4, only flatten when the grouping is unambiguous; preserve profile fields via extensions or manual review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The grouped R6 model better supports rich payload declarations, but removing mandatory R4 paths forces all clients to transform. Keeping deprecated direct fields during a transition would have been less breaking but would require consistency rules between direct and grouped forms.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 `Endpoint.payload` parent is not marked summary even though `payload.type` and `payload.mimeType` are summary children. Implementations that depend on `_summary` extraction should verify actual serializer behavior.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 replaces R4's flat payload fields with grouped payload components. That invalidates untransformed R4 instances because top-level `payloadType` and `payloadMimeType` are no longer the R6 paths, and it changes generated APIs. The redesign has a coherent goal: group type, MIME type, and profile expectations so multiple payload descriptions can be represented without relying on ambiguous cross-products. Keeping the old flat fields in base R6 would ease validation but would duplicate payload metadata and require conflict rules.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Endpoint.payloadType` is a direct 1..* `CodeableConcept` and `Endpoint.payloadMimeType` is a direct 0..* `code`.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Endpoint.payload` is a 0..* `BackboneElement` with `payload.type` and `payload.mimeType` children.
R6 adds `Endpoint.payload.profileCanonical` and `Endpoint.payload.profileUri`, which have no direct base R4 counterpart.
R6 makes the payload group and `payload.type` optional, so R6-to-R4 flattening can require invented or lossy payload type data.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2 and trial-use status are neutral. The model is not highly stable, but the mandatory R4 payload path means the compatibility mechanism is still real.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 top-level payload fields are not valid R6 paths; R6 grouped payloads, profile fields, or missing payload types create R6-to-R4 loss.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could retain deprecated top-level `payloadType` and `payloadMimeType` mapped to a default payload entry. That would preserve many R4 instances, but it would create duplicate flat and grouped payload metadata, ambiguous precedence, and incomplete support for profile-specific or multi-group payload semantics.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the prior report's high impact and Partial alternative judgment are consistent with the direct path removal and the substantial tradeoffs of a dual model.

findings.title: Endpoint.managingOrganization semantics narrow toward technical/help-desk management

oldState.summary: Optional Organization reference for the organization that manages the endpoint, described as the organization associated with the data.

semanticText.short: Organization that manages this endpoint (might not be the organization that exposes the endpoint)
semanticText.definition: The organization that manages this endpoint (even if technically another organization is hosting this in the cloud, it is the organization associated with the data).
semanticText.comment: This property is not typically used when searching for Endpoint resources for usage. The typical usage is via the reference from an applicable Organization/Location/Practitioner resource, which is where the context is provided. Multiple Locations may reference a single endpoint, and don't have to be within the same organization resource, but most likely within the same organizational hierarchy.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 text allowed implementations to read `managingOrganization` as the organization associated with the data even if another entity hosted the endpoint.

newState.summary: Optional Organization reference for the organization providing technical management/help-desk services, explicitly not necessarily the data steward.

semanticText.short: Organization that manages this endpoint (might not be the organization that exposes the endpoint)
semanticText.definition: The organization that provides technical management services for this endpoint.  This would be the organization that acts as the public help desk for when the endpoint is not functioning.  It does NOT necessarily represent the organization who is the steward of data being provided/accepted by the endpoint.
semanticText.comment: This property would NOT be used if the organization is only providing technical infrastructure. For example, it would NOT refer to the cloud hosting provider if that provider were not providing helpdesk support for the endpoint. This property would NOT be used to represent the entity that is the steward of the data exposed by the endpoint.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 reorients the element toward technical management and help-desk responsibility and tells implementers not to use it for data stewardship.

facts.newValue: organization that provides technical management services

facts.oldValue: context typically provided by Organization/Location/Practitioner references
facts.newValue: not the data steward and not merely an infrastructure provider unless providing help desk support

impact.impactRationaleMd: The reference type and cardinality did not change, so validators will not reject old instances solely for this reason. The risk is semantic: directories, routing rules, ownership displays, or support workflows that treated this field as data stewardship may become wrong under R6 conformance text.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Misidentifying the responsible organization can send support, outage, or governance actions to the wrong party.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify that Endpoint itself should identify technical management, while data stewardship comes from directory resources that reference the endpoint.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Preserve the R4 `managingOrganization` meaning and add a distinct optional technical-support or technical-manager organization element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying technical help-desk responsibility is a reasonable goal, but changing the conformance meaning of an unchanged field can break directory governance and support workflows without any validation signal. A base R6 design could have introduced an explicit technical-management organization while leaving the R4 field's data-steward/associated-organization meaning intact. That would meet the new goal with relatively modest tradeoff, so the semantic break looks probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design would retain `managingOrganization` for the R4-era associated organization semantics and add a new optional element for the organization responsible for technical operation or help-desk support. Existing R4 instances would keep their intended meaning, while R6 clients that need the new concept would use the new field. The tradeoff is an additional reference and some transition guidance, but it avoids redefining a populated field in place.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds a new organization reference but avoids silently reinterpreting existing data; long-term cost is moderate model expansion rather than duplicate same-fact encoding.

evidence.detail: R4 describes the referenced organization as associated with the data.
evidence.quote: it is the organization associated with the data

evidence.detail: R6 describes the referenced organization as technical management/help-desk and not necessarily data steward.
evidence.quote: It does NOT necessarily represent the organization who is the steward of data

examples.examplesMd: These fragments remain structurally valid; the incompatibility is semantic. The same reference may be interpreted as data steward in R4-era logic and technical support organization in R6-era logic.

findings.narrativeMd: `Endpoint.managingOrganization` did not change shape, but its conformance meaning changed materially. R4 wording points to the organization associated with the data; R6 points to the organization providing technical management/help-desk services and explicitly excludes data stewardship as the default meaning.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4-valid instance becomes invalid by cardinality or type. The break appears in runtime behavior and governance semantics: code that displays, filters, notifies, or authorizes based on the managing organization may do the wrong thing after an R6 interpretation is applied.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review all uses of `managingOrganization`. If it currently stores data owner/steward, move or derive that relationship through directory resources such as `Organization.endpoint`, `PractitionerRole.endpoint`, or `Location.endpoint`, or preserve a profile/extension. If it stores help-desk responsibility, document that it already aligns with R6.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Clarifying operational responsibility is useful, but changing an existing element's meaning is not fully backward compatible. A separate technical-support organization element would have reduced semantic ambiguity while retaining old data-steward uses.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding requires human review because local directory governance models vary; some R4 implementations may already have used the element in the R6 sense.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This is not a structural validation break, but it changes the meaning of an unchanged field. R4 points implementers toward the organization associated with the data, while R6 describes the technical management or help-desk organization and warns that it is not necessarily the data steward. Existing directory, support, outage, or governance workflows can silently reinterpret old data with no validator signal. A separate technical-management reference would have been a cleaner transition.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Endpoint.managingOrganization` is 0..1 `Reference(Organization)` and describes the organization associated with the data.
R6 StructureDefinition: the same path and type describe technical management/help-desk responsibility and distinguish it from data stewardship.
Cardinality, type, target profile, summary flag, and modifier flag are unchanged, so the compatibility issue is semantic rather than syntactic.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2 and trial-use status are neutral. It does not make every wording change suspect, but the unchanged path plus operational/business responsibility semantics gives this specific text change practical weight.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: the same valid instance can be interpreted as data-steward association in R4-era logic and technical support responsibility in R6-era logic, affecting runtime workflows without a validation error.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. R6 could preserve the R4-era `managingOrganization` meaning and add a new optional technical-manager or support-organization element. The tradeoff is one additional reference and migration guidance, which seems modest compared with redefining a populated field in place.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the prior report's medium semantic impact and Yes less-breaking alternative are well supported; under the fresh rubric this deserves Revisit even though there is no hard instance break.

findings.title: R6 adds Endpoint.environmentType for dev/test/prod classification with no R4 peer

oldState.summary: No local R4 element for endpoint environment classification.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 had no `environmentType`; environment-like semantics were often inferred from `status=test`, endpoint naming, profiles, or extensions.

newState.summary: Optional repeating CodeableConcept bound extensibly to endpoint-environment.

binding.description: The type of environment(s) exposed at this endpoint

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local R6 endpoint-environment CodeSystem is complete and contains prod, staging, dev, test, and train.

semanticText.short: The type of environment(s) exposed at this endpoint
semanticText.definition: The type of environment(s) exposed at this endpoint (dev, prod, test, etc.).

newState.narrativeMd: R6 introduces an explicit environment classification separate from operational status.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Adding an optional element does not invalidate R4 content moving to R6. It does create a down-conversion risk because R4 has no base element for environment classification, and it is closely related to the removed R4 `status=test` code.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Losing environment classification can cause systems to treat a test, staging, or training endpoint like a production endpoint.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent environment classification independently from endpoint availability/status.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is needed because `environmentType` is an optional additive element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: A dedicated environment classification is a reasonable improvement, especially because endpoint environment is not the same as operational availability. The element is optional and additive, so it does not invalidate R4 Endpoint instances moving to R6. The breaking aspect of removing `status=test` is handled by the separate status finding.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Backward-compatible alternative analysis is not applicable to the optional addition itself: base R6 already preserves R4 instances with respect to this element. R4 extensions, naming conventions, or status-code mappings can mitigate R6-to-R4 conversion loss, but those are migration/backport strategies, not less-breaking base R6 designs.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 preservation may require an extension or policy map, but that is a down-conversion mitigation rather than a base R6 alternative.

evidence.detail: R6 adds `Endpoint.environmentType` as 0..* `CodeableConcept` with extensible binding.
The R6 endpoint environment CodeSystem contains prod, staging, dev, test, and train.

examples.examplesMd: Base R4 Endpoint has no environment field; this information needs an extension, profile rule, naming convention, or local mapping.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds `environmentType`, making environment classification first-class. This is likely part of the broader cleanup that removes `status=test`. The addition is not an R4→R6 validation break, but it is important for round-trip conversion and endpoint-directory safety.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances remain valid with respect to this added optional field. R6 instances that use it cannot be represented in base R4 without an extension or convention. Validators will not catch semantic loss if a converter simply drops the field.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When migrating R4 `status=test`, consider whether `environmentType=test` should be populated. When down-converting R6, preserve `environmentType` in an extension and test that production/test filtering behavior remains correct.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The addition itself is compatible in the forward direction and semantically useful. The compatibility problem is mainly due to R4 lacking a peer field and R6 also removing `status=test`.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Review together with the `Endpoint.status` finding; environment classification and operational status should not be conflated.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Endpoint.environmentType` is an optional additive R6 element. It does not invalidate any R4 Endpoint instance moving to R6. It can be important for round-trip or R6-to-R4 conversion, especially because `status=test` moved out of the status code set, but that concern belongs primarily to preservation policy and the separate status-code finding rather than to the optional addition itself.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition has no `Endpoint.environmentType` element.
R6 StructureDefinition adds `Endpoint.environmentType` as 0..* `CodeableConcept` with an extensible binding.
Local R6 CodeSystem-endpoint-environment includes `prod`, `staging`, `dev`, `test`, and `train`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2 and trial-use status are neutral. Because the change is optional and additive, maturity does not create a standards-design concern here.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 environment classifications have no base R4 field, but there is no R4-to-R6 validation, API, or semantic break from adding the optional element.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable. The base R6 design is already forward-compatible for R4 instances. R4 extensions or conversion policy can preserve the new R6 data, but those are mitigations rather than less-breaking R6 base designs.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the prior report correctly notes reverse-conversion loss and no needed less-breaking alternative, but I do not treat this optional addition itself as a medium R4-to-R6 problem.

findings.title: R6 adds Endpoint.availability and narrows Endpoint.period to planned operational interval

oldState.summary: R4 has `Endpoint.period` but no local `availability` element for business hours, transient downtime, or exceptions.

semanticText.short: Interval the endpoint is expected to be operational
semanticText.definition: The interval during which the endpoint is expected to be operational.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 only has the broad `period` element for expected operational interval.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional `Endpoint.availability` of type `Availability`; `period` text says temporary downtime is not represented there.

semanticText.short: Times the endpoint is expected to be available (including exceptions)
semanticText.definition: The times the endpoint is expected to be available, including transient downtimes and any exceptions.
semanticText.comment: Endpoint.availability is meant to represent specific availability, including temporary downtimes or other short term changes in availability. Conversely, Endpoint.period is meant to represent the general planned period of time when the Endpoint may be used.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 separates general planned service period from detailed availability schedules and exceptions.

facts.newValue: Temporary downtimes or other short-term changes in availability would not be represented in this property.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The added optional element does not invalidate R4 data, but it changes the conformance interpretation of `period` and provides an R6-only place for availability schedules and downtime exceptions. Systems that overloaded R4 `period` for schedule-like behavior may need semantic cleanup.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Endpoint availability affects whether clients attempt connections. Losing or misplacing exceptions can cause failed transactions or missed service windows.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent detailed availability schedules and exceptions separately from the endpoint's planned lifecycle period.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `availability` while leaving `period`'s broader R4-era meaning intact or only recommending use of `availability` for schedules.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding `availability` is forward-compatible structurally, but the finding also includes a semantic narrowing of `period` toward planned lifecycle interval rather than temporary downtime or recurring availability. A softer base design could have added `availability` while preserving broader `period` interpretation, but that would weaken the clean separation that generic R6 clients need. Given the ambiguity and limited expressive power of a single `Period`, the R6 clarification is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design would add the optional `Availability` element and describe it as the preferred or more precise place for business hours and exceptions, without saying that short-term availability is outside `period`. That would preserve R4 systems that treated `period` broadly. The tradeoff is material: `period` cannot represent recurring hours or exception details, and leaving its meaning broad would keep validation and client behavior ambiguous.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would reduce semantic disruption for overloaded R4 `period` use but leaves ambiguity between lifecycle period and detailed availability.

evidence.detail: R6 says temporary downtimes or short-term availability changes are not represented in `period`.

examples.examplesMd: The structure of `Availability` is illustrative and should be checked against the separate R6 `Availability` datatype report.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds `Endpoint.availability` for detailed availability and explicitly says `period` is not for temporary downtime or short-term availability. This creates a new model for operational scheduling and can invalidate assumptions in systems that used R4 `period` as a broad availability field.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: There is no forward hard validation break because the element is optional. R6 instances that carry availability schedules lose information when converted to base R4. R4-era business rules over `period` may still run but produce behavior that is semantically different from R6 guidance.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review any R4 `period` usage that encodes business hours or temporary downtime and migrate it to `availability` where possible. Down-conversion should preserve `availability` in an extension or omit it only with an explicit loss-of-information warning.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The new element is justified by clearer modeling. A standard extension would be the backward-compatible route for R4, but it would not be as visible to generic clients as a base element.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The `Availability` datatype itself is outside this report and should be reviewed for additional datatype-level changes.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The new `availability` element is optional, so there is no direct old-valid/new-invalid instance break. The compatibility issue is semantic: R6 adds a schedule/exception home and narrows `period` toward the general planned lifecycle of the endpoint. R4 systems that used `period` for downtime or availability windows need review, and R6 availability details cannot be represented in base R4. The change is still proportionate because a single `Period` cannot model recurring hours or exceptions well, and keeping both meanings broad would preserve ambiguity for generic clients.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Endpoint.period` is 0..1 `Period` with a broad expected-operational-interval definition.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Endpoint.availability` is added as 0..1 `Availability` for expected availability, transient downtime, and exceptions.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Endpoint.period` comment says temporary downtimes or short-term availability changes are not represented in `period`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2 and trial-use status are neutral. The semantic migration concern matters, but the maturity level does not require preserving an ambiguous R4 use at the expense of a clearer R6 model.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: old `period` content remains structurally valid but may no longer carry the same intended availability meaning; R6-to-R4 loss also occurs for `availability` schedules and exceptions.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could add `availability` while leaving `period` broadly described as any operational interval. That would reduce semantic disruption for overloaded R4 uses, but it would weaken the separation between lifecycle period and detailed availability and leave generic clients unsure which element to trust.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the prior report's medium impact and Partial alternative judgment fit the evidence; the fresh judgment is that the break is real but proportionate.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R6 StructureDefinition exists with the same canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, base definition, and abstract flag. Artifact status changed from draft to active and is recorded as a notable non-breaking change.

For unchanged local paths, cardinalities are stable: `identifier`, `status`, `name`, `managingOrganization`, `contact`, `period`, `address`, and `header`. Cardinality changes for `connectionType` and payload are captured in findings.
`Endpoint.managingOrganization` remains `Reference(Organization)`. No local Endpoint reference target expansion or narrowing was found.
No Endpoint-specific invariant beyond inherited `ele-1`/`dom-*` constraints was found. Base constraint expression changes are out of scope for this Endpoint report.
No local fixed, pattern, or default values were found on Endpoint elements.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex value limits were found on Endpoint elements.
No local slicing definitions were found for Endpoint in either version.
`Endpoint.status` remains a modifier with the same modifier reason. New `Endpoint.payload.modifierExtension` is inherited from BackboneElement and not treated as a local Endpoint modifier finding.

Material binding changes for `status`, `connectionType`, payload type, and `environmentType` are captured in findings. The MIME type value set compose remains `urn:ietf:bcp:13` in both versions. External terminology expansions were not available for every included system.

Local unchanged paths keep the same datatypes for `identifier`, `status`, `name`, `managingOrganization`, `contact`, `period`, `address`, and `header`. Type changes for `connectionType`, payload, and new R6 fields are captured in findings.

Local summary intent is broadly stable for unchanged fields. New R6 summary fields include `description`, `environmentType`, `payload.type`, and `payload.mimeType`; payload movement is covered in the payload finding. Inherited summary flag changes on base elements are out of scope.
No resource identity serialization change was found. Serialization breaks are limited to local element shape/path changes already captured for `connectionType` and payload.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Artifact publication status does not change instance wire format, validation cardinality, datatype, or terminology by itself.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Treat this as a maturity signal for R6 Endpoint, not an instance transform requirement.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds optional Endpoint.description
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `description` is optional `0..1 string`, so R4 instances remain valid with respect to this addition and no existing R4 element is removed solely for this feature.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Down-conversion to R4 needs an extension or omission if descriptions must be preserved.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Endpoint.contact definition now says endpoint instead of subscription
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element path, cardinality, datatype, and flags are unchanged. The R4 text appears to have a copy/paste reference to subscription, while R6 corrects it to endpoint.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: No transform is needed, but documentation generated from R6 will read more accurately.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: MIME type binding remains required to the same BCP13 value set compose
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Although the element moved under `payload`, the local `ValueSet-mimetypes.json` compose still includes `urn:ietf:bcp:13` in both packages. No local evidence of a MIME type code narrowing was found.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: The binding target version changes from 4.0.1 to 6.0.0-ballot4 as part of the versioned R6 element; exact expansions were not available.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Inherited base changes such as `language` binding, base constraints, extension constraints, and summary flags were observed in snapshots but intentionally excluded from local Endpoint findings.
`Endpoint.availability` is new in R6 and depends on the R6 `Availability` datatype. Datatype-level breaking changes and exact representability should be handled in that datatype's report.
The R6 payload type value set compose now includes external `v3-HL7FormatCodes`; authoritative expansion would clarify exact code-level changes for payload migration.

`connectionType` binding strength weakens and the local R6 core package does not include the external THO CodeSystem content, so terminology-specific migration guidance needs the terminology package or server.
